chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

regarding the one who dyes his head with henna, then it becomes inevitable for him with regards to the Ablution (Wudu). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not allowed until he pours water onto the skin of his head.'

key_terms.الْحِنَّاءِ: Henna, a natural dye used for coloring hair and skin.
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: Ablution, the ritual washing required before prayer.
key_terms.بَشَرَةَ: Skin, specifically referring to the skin of the head which must be wetted during wudu.
key_terms.يَخْضِبُ: To dye, specifically referring to the act of applying henna.

ai.seo_question: Does henna on the head invalidate wudu if it blocks water from reaching the skin?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the condition of *masah* (wiping) in wudu by distinguishing between mere coloration and a physical barrier (*hudh*) that prevents water from reaching the skin. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that henna is permissible for worship as long as it does not form a thick layer that blocks water, reflecting the principle that ritual purity requires direct contact of water with the skin unless a valid excuse exists.
